questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: You should increase your following distance when towing a trailer. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What should be part of your normal scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while riding. Always check them before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view ahead and helps other drivers see that you plan to pass.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without interfering with your control, and hold onto passenger handholds, your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help maintain control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before entering the turn. Look through the turn toward where you want to go, lean by pressing the handlebar, and gently roll on the throttle to stabilize the suspension.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors provide?

options.text: A narrow view of the road behind you.
A wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: A wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view than flat mirrors. Objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.

questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slowly approach it. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not kick the dog.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. This is safest. Riding on the side closest to the passing car increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle rider safely turn?

options.text: Lean in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: What should you wear while riding?

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent this damage.

questions.question: What is the minimum safe following distance under normal conditions?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface coming up.
Road conditions that stay the same as you approach them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions that stay the same as you approach them.
questions.explanation: Look for problems on the road. Make a plan to handle them safely.

questions.question: What does this yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane, what happens?

options.text: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important for helmet protection?
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly all around, and have no damage like cracks or loose padding.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which lane position is safest?

options.text: The left side of your lane.
The right side of your lane.

questions.explanation: The center of your lane is safest when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger to do on your motorcycle?

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine is running. They should sit as far forward as comfortable, not crowding you.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help protect you from serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects against injury. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what traffic rules apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift immediately to a lower gear.
Proceed in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: When your motorcycle weaves on uneven gratings, stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Do not swerve side to side, as this is more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch for changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through grooved pavement. Ride slowly across the grooves.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
It applies brakes automatically based on your riding habits.
It connects to the gears and brakes when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use the rear brake, both brakes work together. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's specific braking system.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes, during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help you avoid a crash?

options.text: Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: Always stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, beside, and behind you.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight across angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle may move you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection every time you ride.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as possible.
